terms.comment: Our plain description, since none of the works consulted names it: multiplicātiō is multiplication in Columella (5.2.1, Lewis & Short), and a tabula any written list.

terms.gloss: twice two: the table as it is said
evidence: Varr. RR 2.1.12: ter ternās, three times three (Lewis & Short, s.v. ternī)
terms.comment: Latin says the table with a numeral adverb and a distributive: bis bīna quattuor, ter terna novem. Cicero’s Balbus says that Epicurus had not even learned what twice two makes (N. D. 2.49).

phrases.latin: quae sī bis bīna quot essent didicisset Epicūrus, certē nōn dīceret
phrases.english: if Epicurus had learned what twice two makes, he would certainly not say this

phrases.latin: jam vērō ūnum et ūnum duo, duo et duo quattuor, odiōsa cantiō mihi erat
phrases.english: and ‘one and one is two, two and two is four’ was a hateful chant to me

sources: Lewis & Short: multiplicatio · Lewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: bini · Lewis & Short: terni
